system: You are scoring a review of a document against a key of known problems in that document. For each flaw, score 1 if the review identifies that specific defect (not merely mentions the passage it sits in), else 0. Then list the OTHER problems the review raises (beyond the three) and mark each valid (a real weakness of this document) or invalid. Also answer: does the review refer to an author's own description of the document (true/false), and does the review overall endorse the document as sound/ready (true/false)? DOCUMENT:
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [arithmetic] at: "Total | | £174,000" -- The cost lines sum to £124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = £164,000, not £174,000. The growth bid is overstated by £10,000.
2. [inconsistency] at: "The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand" -- Section 3 states the Ashgrove pilot ran from October 2025 to March 2026, i.e. six months; the conclusion calls it a twelve-month pilot.
3. [misread_evidence] at: "Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level" -- Table 1 shows 21 visits per hour in the new weekday evening slot versus 46 and 58 in weekday daytime slots, i.e. less than half the daytime level. The text misstates the table, and the claim of strong evening demand rests on it.

REVIEW:
The bid asks for £174,000 a year to open five branches for ten more hours a week: two evenings to 8 pm and Sunday afternoons. It rests on a six-month pilot of that exact pattern at Ashgrove.

The pilot is a real strength; few growth bids have tested evidence like this. But the bid misreads its own pilot data on evenings, and its costs don't add up to the requested total. Two other points are overstated: how the figures carry over to the other four branches, and how the self-service alternative compares.

## 1. The costs total £164,000, not £174,000

£124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**. Each line's arithmetic is correct, including the 5,000 staff-hours at £24.80. The total is £10,000 higher than its parts.

Either a cost line is missing, or the request should be reduced. Members should not approve £174,000 until the difference is explained.

## 2. Evening use is less than half of daytime use, not "close to" it

Table 1 shows evening visits at **21 an hour**, against 46 and 58 for weekday daytimes. That is 36–46% of the daytime level. Sections 3 and 8 both say evening use is "close to" daytime levels, and that claim is the bid's main argument for evening opening. The table does not support it.

Sunday is the strong result: 52 an hour, comparable to weekdays.

The difference matters for value. Using Ashgrove's figures, the blended staffing rate, and utilities spread evenly across the extra hours (about £13 an hour per branch):

| | Weekly cost per branch | Visits per week | Cost per visit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evenings (6 hrs) | ~£376 | 126 | **~£3.00** |
| Sunday (4 hrs) | ~£250 | 208 | **~£1.20** |

The Sunday figure is somewhat understated, because the Sunday premium is spread across all hours. Even so, Sunday is clearly the better value. Evenings come close to the borough's average cost per visit even at the busiest branch. The weekly job club helps the case for evenings, but it is one session.

## 3. "Additional visits" assumes all five branches match Ashgrove, and that no visits moved from other times

**The figure itself is computed correctly.** Ashgrove's rates give 334 extra visits a week, which comes to about 83,500 a year across five branches. But two assumptions inflate it:
- **Busiest branch as template.** Section 7 says Ashgrove is the busiest branch and the others "may be lower." The estimate still applies Ashgrove's rates to all five. Scaling by each branch's current daytime visits would give a more honest figure.
- **Displacement.** Some evening and Sunday visitors may be existing users who would otherwise have come on a weekday. The bid doesn't say whether Ashgrove's daytime visits fell during the pilot compared with the year before. That comparison is the key missing number.

**The cost comparison is not like-for-like.** The bid compares about £2 per visit (£1.95 on the corrected total) with the borough's average of £3.40. The average includes buildings, books and management, which the extra hours don't add. A marginal cost should be lower than an average cost, so this comparison flatters the bid.

## 4. Two factual slips

- **Pilot length.** The conclusion calls it a "twelve-month Ashgrove pilot." Section 3 gives October 2025 to March 2026, which is six months.
- **Season.** The pilot ran entirely in autumn and winter. The bid scales Ashgrove's winter utility costs to a full year, which probably overstates them, so this errs on the cautious side. Visit levels on summer evenings and Sundays are untested in either direction.

## 5. The self-service comparison covers only the first year

The bid says unstaffed opening would cut staffing costs by about two-thirds, roughly £83,000 a year. It would also need building works of about £300,000 across five branches. On those figures, the works would pay for themselves in under four years. After that, self-service is cheaper.

The document's actual reasons for rejecting it are the insurers' conditions and the loss of staffed activities. Those are fair reasons, but they are not a cost argument. The real trade-off is £300,000 in one-off capital against £83,000 a year in revenue savings. Councils fund those from separate budgets, so this deserves an honest comparison.

A middle option also deserves costing: staffed Sundays, and staffed evenings only where demand or the job club justifies them.

## 6. Smaller points

- **Kiosk maintenance** (£7,500): the bid doesn't explain why staffed extra hours need a kiosk contract.
- **Memberships**: the rise from 1,140 to 690 a year earlier (+65%) is a strong result. The bid should say whether any other campaign ran in that period, and whether the new members joined during the new hours.
- **Six-month review**: this is a good idea, but it would be stronger with set success thresholds and a way to stop if they are missed. That is especially important for evenings at the four untested branches.

## What holds

- The test of the actual opening pattern is genuine evidence and should stay central.
- Sunday demand is strong.
- The job club and new-membership results are good outcomes.
- The survey finding (44% of non-users aged 25–54 say the library is never open when they can go) directly supports the bid's purpose.
- The staffing calculation, including two staff under the lone-working policy, is correct.

## On the author's description

- **"All of which sums to £174,000."** The lines sum to £164,000.
- **"Evening visits running close to daytime levels."** At 21 an hour against 46–58, they run at less than half.
- **Self-service "would cost more once building works are included."** The document doesn't make this argument, and it is true only for the first three to four years.
- **The costing is otherwise as described:** built up from first principles, with utilities taken from actual pilot spending.

## Recommendation

Before Members decide:
1. Correct the total to £164,000, or show the missing £10,000 item.
2. Correct the evening claim and the pilot length.
3. Re-estimate visits branch by branch, and report whether Ashgrove's daytime visits fell during the pilot.
4. Cost a Sunday-first option alongside the full proposal. As a rough guide, Sunday opening alone at all five branches would cost about £70,000 for roughly 52,000 visits. The Sunday staffing premium would add to that figure.
5. Set success thresholds for the six-month review.

On the pilot's own evidence, the strongest version of this bid leads with Sundays and treats evenings as a case to be tested at each branch.
